notes: Test prompts for iterating on this skill via skill-creator. Outputs are prose notes, so grading is mostly qualitative — the objective assertions below are the ones scripts/check_note.py can verify mechanically.

evals.name: rough-draft-preservation
evals.prompt: amar 1.6 er props README ta ekta draft kore rekhechi, oita enhance kore dao
evals.expected_output: Every bullet from the rough draft survives as a section in the enhanced note, expanded with a Bangla explanation, an analogy, and a code example drawn from the actual files in the topic folder. A JavaScript Prerequisites section links object destructuring back to module-0/js-refresher.
assertions: Every original bullet from the draft is still present in some form
Bangla prose ratio measures between 45% and 80%
Technical terms (props, state, component, render) remain in English
Note references at least one real filename from the topic folder
Contains 5-6 interview questions written in English

evals.name: factually-wrong-point-flagged
evals.prompt: enhance this note - i wrote that props can be changed by the child component if you use setState inside it
evals.expected_output: The note carries the corrected explanation (props are read-only; changes belong in the parent's state), AND the chat reply explicitly tells the user their point was wrong and why. The wrong claim is not silently deleted without comment.
assertions: Note contains the correct read-only explanation
Chat reply explicitly flags the misconception and explains why it is wrong
The correction is surfaced in chat, not only silently fixed in the file

evals.name: english-heavy-tooling-topic
evals.prompt: write the readme for the install-react folder
evals.expected_output: A tooling topic where most content is legitimately English (npm commands, config keys, extension names). The skill should not pad the note with filler Bangla to hit the ratio; it should explain the setup steps in Bangla where explanation is actually needed and say in chat that the ratio is low for a valid reason.
assertions: Bangla is used for explanation of why steps matter, not mechanically inserted
No filler Bangla added purely to move the ratio
Chat reply acknowledges the ratio is legitimately low for a tooling topic
